CANDIDATE bd-01M14YJ8FG15S0R1ART7DTM1XZ W4(10) embed-bench: 210919f on branch m1/embed-bench, rebased cleanly onto current main (96a59aa, contains the landed wire slice). Not merged. 12 files added + build.sbt (1606 lines Scala): embed-bench/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/bench/{gold,origin,case,channels,metrics,report,wog}.scala; tests {MetricsSuite, LabelSuite, ProtocolSuite, WogDiagnosticSuite}; embed-bench/README.md.

GATE at the clean pin (0329c43): scalafmtCheckAll success, scalafmtSbtCheck success, compileAll success on all three platforms, embedBench/test Passed: Total 25, Failed 0 (LabelSuite 9, WogDiagnosticSuite 8, MetricsSuite 6, ProtocolSuite 2). Exit 0. No embed-bench warnings.

BUILD.SBT hunk is exactly the announced one plus the aggregate wiring: a new lazy val embedBench = project.in(file("embed-bench")) with commonSettings, name storymodel4s-embed-bench, dependsOn(embedCore.jvm, embedGrakern, align.jvm, fixtures.jvm, laws.jvm % Test); embedBench added to the aggregate list; jvmOnlyModules becomes List("embedGrakern", "embedBench") so compileAll/testAll/testJVM pick it up. No new library. Note for codex-storymodel4s-root: this touches build.sbt, so whoever lands second rebases the one-line hunk, as the chief sequenced.

DESIGN CHOICES where the spike spec was open (chief, please correct any you disagree with):
1. Frozen-set loading needs the codec, which embed-bench does not depend on. Split: FrozenManifest is the typed value the codec will produce; FrozenSet.verify(manifest, read) owns the FREEZE rule (every file present and matching, set id carrying the manifest-checksum suffix, every story partitioned). No JSON parsing in the bench, no codec dependency, and the rule is testable today with no frozen set in existence.
2. Protocol pin: ProtocolDocument.pinned is a constant (canonical-text SHA-256 of the adjudication protocol doc) and ProtocolSuite RECOMPUTES it from docs/plans/, so an unannounced protocol edit fails the build instead of silently drifting - this is the mechanism behind the manifest's protocolChecksum rule.
3. No Defaults API in this slice, deliberately, documented in the README and BenchReport Scaladoc: selecting a tier default needs the untouched-test partition of a frozen set and none is frozen. Calibrated is unreachable until an adjudicated set exists; drift or diagnostic origin fails closed to Diagnostic with a typed reason.
4. Ranking for recall@k / MRR ranks anchored states only - externals are destinations, not candidates - so an external MAP with the target ranked first still scores recall@1 = 1 among anchors, and open-world behaviour is reported by its own metrics, never pooled (design contract 6 and 7).
5. Aggregation is story-macro (mean of per-case means) per the spec's macro CIs; a case with no eligible unit contributes no mean but still counts in Coverage.eligible, so "not applicable" never reads as zero.
6. WOG's view carries no proposition charts, so grakern d_wl has nothing to prepare; rather than a zero-scoring stub the channel reports StructuralIdentity.Absent(reason) with structural coverage 0. The grakern path is exercised whenever a view does carry charts.

FLAG outside this bead's paths, for the fixtures owner: WarOfTheGhostsModel has a class-initialization order hazard - touching WarOfTheGhostsExpectations (hence the nested S/G id objects) before the outer object yields null-derived ids and a validation failure ("2 claims share id ... null"). Worked around in WogDiagnostic by forcing WarOfTheGhostsModel.model first, with a Scaladoc note; the fixture should be made order-independent by whoever owns it. Happy to take that as a small bead.
